quests.title: See if you can spot a bicycle at Springbank Park today.
quests.note: Any safe, accessible spot in the park counts. Stay on public paths.
tidbits: Springbank Park offers wide paths for rolling along at an easy pace.

quests.title: See if you can spot a bicycle over at Gibbons Park today.
quests.note: Any safe, accessible spot in the park counts. Stay on public paths.
tidbits: The Thames River cuts right past this green space, so we might hear water before we see wheels.
Bicycles have been helping people roll down park paths for generations now.
If we keep our pace steady, finding that bike should be a nice quiet puzzle.

quests.title: Find a bicycle at Victoria Park, with a friend.
quests.note: Any safe, accessible spot in the park counts. Stay on public paths.
tidbits: Park paths usually follow the easiest slope, which suits four legs and two legs alike.
Bicycles were originally called velocipedes before people shortened the name.
A park is simply a patch of open green kept quiet amidst the noise of the city.

quests.title: See if you can spot a tree at Longwoods Road Conservation Area.
quests.note: Stay on the marked trail. Any safe, accessible spot counts.
tidbits: Trees spend centuries standing still while the whole forest shifts around them.
That thick bark protects the inner wood from weather and hungry visitors alike.

quests.title: See if a duck is lingering near Sifton Bog Trail today.
quests.note: Stay on the marked trail. Any safe, accessible spot counts.
tidbits: A bog floor is made of thick peat, which holds onto a lot of water.
Ducks have special glands near their tails to keep their feathers waterproof.
Sometimes solitary ducks just like to float quietly in the shade of the reeds.

quests.title: Go find a squirrel at Boler Mountain with a friend.
quests.note: Stay on the marked trail. Any safe, accessible spot counts.
tidbits: Grey squirrels like this area often bury many different nuts and remember where most of them are hidden.
Tree branches up ahead make fine highways for bushy tails if we keep our eyes on the canopy.
Squirrel whiskers help them balance as they scramble along narrow wooden rails.

quests.title: See if you can spot a squirrel at Byron Valley today.
quests.note: Stay on the marked trail. Any safe, accessible spot counts.
tidbits: Grey squirrels like this one often bury dozens of nuts and actually remember where most of them are hidden.
Byron Valley gives us a fine, quiet stretch of green where the trees keep us company all the way.
A squirrel tail serves as a handy balance pole when they are scampering along high branches.

quests.title: See if you can spot a squirrel at The Coves today.
quests.note: Stay on the marked trail. Any safe, accessible spot counts.
tidbits: Squirrels spend a lot of their time burying acorns and then trying to remember where they put them.
River valleys like this one are great quiet places to look up and watch the trees.
Grey squirrels can jump quite far between branches without making much of a sound.

quests.title: Find a tree at Kains Woods, with a friend.
quests.note: Stay on the marked trail. Any safe, accessible spot counts.
tidbits: The river valley holds the mist close to the ground today.
Trees are patient listeners when we take our time walking.
